audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill / Malphite / Malphite / Skill / Skill / Malphite / Malphite, which contradicts the already-audited mirror at four stages.
audit.why: audits/top/zac__malphite.json settled this direction as five Skill stages through laning and then Zac at First item and Two+ items, on the strength of Zac's 55.75% over 287 games from his side. Reused rather than re-derived. It is also what this page's own whys say: whys[0] calls level 1 even, whys[2] says "Still even", and whys[6] says his sustain "reclaim[s] parity late" — while the chart hands Malphite levels 2, 3 and both item stages. The mechanics behind Zac owning the item stages are the two the mirror identified: Unstable Matter burns percent maximum health against the champion who stacks health and armour, and Let's Bounce! returns ten seconds sooner than Unstoppable Force at every rank.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Zac / Zac — the exact inverse of the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield is leaned on in four separate fields — "Eat Granite Shield procs by stepping out after he commits", "Granite Shield plus your first armor item" — and nothing says under what condition it comes back.
audit.why: It recharges only if Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds. Unstable Matter is a flat 5-second cooldown at every rank, costs him nothing, and needs only proximity. Zac is therefore the best-equipped champion in the game to switch your passive off permanently, and "step out after he commits" is advice that does not work against a button he can press purely to tick you. Worse, the same ability deals percent MAXIMUM health, so the armour-and-health plan the entry recommends is the thing feeding it. This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Stated from your side in early, mid, spikes[2], whys[3] and whys[6] — the mirror states the same fact from Zac's.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] both present Unstoppable Force as a clean level-6 takeover: "an unblinkable knock-up into a dashless tank — R his sling commitment and you own the all-in".
audit.why: The first half survives — the mirror also concluded that a knock-up stops his bounces, so your R does beat Let's Bounce! head-on. But Zac is not dashless: Elastic Slingshot is a dash on 21 seconds falling to 9. And the ultimate arithmetic runs against you, which is the part that decides games rather than single fights: Let's Bounce! is 120/105/90 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100, ten seconds shorter at every single rank. You win the first exchange of ultimates and he is ready for the second one first.
audit.corrected: The 10-second gap added to spikes[1], mid and whys[6]; Elastic Slingshot given its real cooldown in whys[1] and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: "Bait the E sling, then punish the long cooldown" never says how long, and nothing anywhere mentions resources.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21 seconds at rank 1 and still 9 at rank 5, so early it is a genuine twenty-second punish window and late it is barely one — the advice ages badly without the number. The resource asymmetry is the other half: every Zac ability costs a share of his current health and no mana at all, while Seismic Shard alone is 70 to 90 mana on an 8-second cooldown. In a farm lane decided by who can keep pressing buttons, he can afford to throw Unstable Matter purely to deny your shield and you cannot afford to answer in kind.
audit.corrected: Cooldown and the mana-versus-no-mana asymmetry added to early, whys[1] and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Zac's damage is called "even AD" three times — "out-trading his even AD damage", "his straight AD trades can't crack", "past his even AD trades".
audit.why: Unstable Matter deals magic damage as a percentage of maximum health, which is neither AD nor reducible by the armour the entry keeps recommending against it. Armour is still right for the rest of the lane, but the field that tells you armour answers his trades is naming the wrong damage type and pointing at the wrong ability. Cell Division is also a heal on every ability hit, which is what actually makes his laning unpunishable by chip.
audit.corrected: "Even AD" replaced with the percent-health description in mid, late and whys[5].
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W percent maximum health magic damage; P "sheds a chunk of himself that can be reabsorbed to restore Health")

edits.before: Pre-6 you have no trade pattern and Zac out-sustains you with his passive blobs, so don't try to win the lane — just CS and respect his E sling. His sling is the real danger: it lets him pull you off the wave or all-in with Q/W CC before your W and E exist, and he can pick up blobs to undo any poke you land. Eat Granite Shield procs by stepping out after he commits, and never stand in a spot where a sling-in lets him CC you into a gank.
edits.after: Pre-6 you have no trade pattern and Cell Division heals him off every ability hit, so don't try to win the lane — CS and respect Elastic Slingshot, a 21-second dash at rank 1 that pulls you off the wave into his Q and W. The bad news about "step out and let Granite Shield recharge": Unstable Matter is a free 5-second pulse, so he can deny the recharge at no cost while Seismic Shard costs you 70 mana a cast.

edits.before: This is where you stabilize and then take over. W Thunderclap's bonus armor plus its empowered AoE autos and E Ground Slam's attack-speed slow let you farm through his shove and start out-trading his even AD damage. Level 6 is your real spike: Unstoppable Force has no counterplay for a tank with no dash — if he slings in to commit, R him up isolated before his blobs reattach, or hold it to flank his back line. Bait the E sling, then punish the long cooldown.
edits.after: This is where you stabilize. Thunderclap's armour and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow let you farm through his shove, but be clear about what armour does not answer — Unstable Matter is percent maximum health. Level 6 is a real spike with a real limit: a knock-up stops his bounces, so you win the first ult trade outright, and then Let's Bounce! comes back at 120 seconds against your 130. Bait the sling and punish its 21-second cooldown.

edits.before: Once your armor items come online your E and W scale into a wall his straight AD trades can't crack, and Q's slow plus move-speed steal shuts down his sling re-engages. But Zac is a tank too, so this never becomes a 1v1 stomp — it trades evenly and swings on R usage. Your job late is teamfight engage: land Unstoppable Force on his carries, not on Zac, since he just bounces and reattaches. Win the fight, not the duel.
edits.after: Armour scales Ground Slam and shuts down his sling re-engages with Seismic Shard's speed steal — but it is the wrong answer to percent maximum health, and stacking it hands Unstable Matter a bigger number every item. His 5-second pulse also means Granite Shield simply never comes back mid-fight. Land Unstoppable Force on his carries, not on Zac, who bounces and reattaches. Win the fight, not the duel.

edits.before: His E sling plus Q/W CC is the only thing that swings this stage; you have no W/E yet, so don't get pulled off-wave.
edits.after: Elastic Slingshot is a 21s dash into Q and W CC, and nothing he casts costs mana — don't get pulled off the wave.

edits.before: W Thunderclap's armor and E Ground Slam's attack-speed slow come up and even the trades, but he sustains it back — genuinely split.
edits.after: Thunderclap and Ground Slam even the trades, but Unstable Matter pulses every 5s so Granite Shield never recharges — split.

edits.before: Granite Shield plus your first armor item makes E and W scale past his even AD trades — this is your power window.
edits.after: Your armor scales Ground Slam, but Unstable Matter reads maximum health — stacking is what he wants you to do.

edits.before: His passive blob sustain and even tank trades reclaim parity late — it swings on R targeting, not a duel, so play the teamfight.
edits.after: Let's Bounce! is 10s shorter than your R at every rank and Cell Division heals him back — play the teamfight, not the duel.

notes: This direction is written to agree with audits/top/zac__malphite.json, which was already on disk. The mechanical findings there are reused rather than re-derived: the Granite-Shield-versus-Unstable-Matter denial, the 120-vs-130 ultimate gap, the mana asymmetry, and the conclusion that a knock-up does stop Let's Bounce!. Ratings are inverse and the chart is the exact mirror. Two carried-over cautions I honoured. (1) Zac's E carries a "grounding" flag in the kit file, and _missing-interactions.json builds a claim on it that Elastic Slingshot shuts off Unstoppable Force — the mirror judged that flag a parsing artefact of "attaches his arms to the ground", and I wrote nothing based on it. (2) Malphite's own Q and E carry the same bogus grounding flag and his R a bogus projectile flag; none of them appear in my text. Finally, all three suspectNames the packet raised for this matchup — "Seismic Shard's", "Eat Granite Shield", "Ground Slam's" — are false positives; those are Malphite's real ability names and the checker is tripping on possessives and on the verb in front.
